newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opens bidding for short railroad lines.
newsitem.headline: Mexico opens bidding for short railroad lines.

text.p: Mexico's Communication and Transport Ministry said it opened the bidding process for three short railroad lines as part of the privatization of Mexico's rail system, the ministry said in the Official Gazette on Thursday.
The lines include 71.4 kilometers of track from Tijuana to Tecate in Baja California and 320.3 km Nacozari route in Sonora state and 973.9 km of rail from Coahuila to Durango.
The Baja California track runs along the U.S. border with California and the Nacozari route run along the U.S. border with Arizona from Nogales to Agua Prieta and Nacozari.
The Coahuila-Durango route runs through four states in the center of Mexico.
Applications to file a bid will be due on May 7 with a decision expected after June 6, the ministry said.

The routes connect with Mexico's largest railroad line, the Pacific-North, a more than 6,000 km line that connects ports from both sides of the nations with five border entry points and major city centers.
Bids for the Pacific-North line are due on June 19 will a winner expected announced July 7.
Bidding companies include: Union Pacific Corp. with Empresas ICA ; Grupo Mexico ; and Grupo Tribasa with local ITISA and Railtex Service Co.
